2. ANALYSIS CHECK: These explanation sentences just restate the evidence. Improve each: a) 'According to WWF, 8 million tonnes of plastic enter the ocean yearly. This means there is a lot of plastic.' → b) 'Dolphins are very intelligent. This shows dolphins are smart.'

3. MATH SPIRAL: Your data table shows: Plastic found in ocean in 2010: 5 million tonnes, 2015: 7 million tonnes, 2020: 9 million tonnes. Calculate: What is the rate of increase per 5 years? At this rate, what will the 2025 figure be?

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Revision is different from editing. REVISION means changing the BIG PICTURE — improving your ideas, arguments, evidence, and structure. EDITING means fixing small mistakes — grammar, spelling, punctuation.
content: 📖 Revision is different from editing. REVISION means changing the BIG PICTURE — improving your ideas, arguments, evidence, and structure. EDITING means fixing small mistakes — grammar, spelling, punctuation.
Professional writers always revise BEFORE they edit. There is no point fixing the grammar in a paragraph you are going to delete!

In content revision, you ask these questions: Is my thesis argument clearly proven by the body paragraphs? Does each body paragraph have a clear POINT? Is my EVIDENCE strong and from reliable sources? Does my EXPLANATION actually analyze the evidence, or just repeat it? Are my TRANSITIONS smooth and logical?

During this lesson, you will revise your report based on peer feedback from W112. Focus on the TOP 3 improvements from your revision plan. Remember: it is always better to write LESS but more precisely than to add lots of extra sentences that say nothing new.
